candidate_analysis.explanation: The Random Forest assigns a 0.99 malware probability, and all 20 top SHAP features push toward cryptojacking. The contributions are diffuse, between +0.0067 and +0.0129, so no single feature dominates. The verdict rests on the combined weight of many weak signals. Two groups of n-grams stand out. The first is arithmetic and bit-manipulation sequences typical of hash and cipher inner loops: ADD ROR (+0.008333), MOV ROL (+0.008013), XOR ADC (+0.006813), DIV MUL (+0.007087), POP XOR (+0.012068) and POP SUB (+0.012048). Rotates, XOR and carry-propagating arithmetic are characteristic of mining-style hashing or big-number routines, although the evidence does not name the algorithm. These sequences are rare (frequencies 0.000035 to 0.000282), so the model is picking up distinctive, low-frequency code. The second group is stack-heavy sequences with high frequency: LEA PUSH (0.028627), MOV PUSH (0.038020), ADD PUSH (0.015065), SUB PUSH (0.014583), CALL PUSH, POP PUSH, INC PUSH and MOVZX PUSH. These suggest a 32-bit stack-passing calling convention with many call sites and argument setups. On their own they are generic compiler output, but their large combined SHAP contribution means the model associates this code-density profile with the malware class. LEA MOVSD.REP (+0.007936) indicates block memory copy or initialization, and FSTP MOV (+0.007274) indicates some x87 floating-point use. No function-level attribution, strings or API evidence was provided, so the verdict cannot be tied to specific mining behavior such as stratum or pool communication. The classification is therefore high-confidence on the strength of the model output and the crypto-style arithmetic n-grams, with the generic stack patterns as weaker support.
